about: The pre-registered pairwise key (docs/SIMILARITY-LITERATURE.md, step 4): drug pairs whose relationship is settled, each citing sources a reader can check. Graded by analysis/answer_keys/pairs.mjs under the rules below, which were fixed with the pairs and before either graded the ranking. Held out: never a target for a sweep. A change to a pair or a rule is a new version, logged in docs/SIMILARITY-HARNESS.md, and is never made in the same change as a constant it judges.

rules.directions: Each pair is read both ways: b in a's list and a in b's.
rules.positive: The same primary mechanism at the same target(s), in the same direction. A hit when the partner ranks within top_k; a partner absent from the list shares no target and is unreachable, reported apart and never a miss.
rules.negative: Known-unlike: the same indication by different primary mechanisms with no shared primary target. Clean when the partner ranks below top_k or is absent.
rules.opposite: One target, opposite directions (agonist against antagonist or inverse agonist, positive against negative modulation). Clean when the partner ranks below top_k or is absent.
rules.ordering: For each list asked about at least one reachable positive and at least one negative or opposite: the share of (positive, other) pairs in which the positive ranks higher, an absent partner ranking below everything and a tie counting half; averaged over lists.
rules.readings: Three, all reported: every pair; without the pairs marked seen; without the pairs marked doubt. None replaces another.

provenance.written: Drafted on 2026-10-14 by three subagents, one per area (psychiatry; neurology and pain; autonomic and other receptor systems), each given only the catalogue's ChEMBL ids and names and forbidden to open the repository or run the ranking; reviewed and edited by the session that commissioned them, which had not graded the ranking against any pair before this file was committed.
provenance.sources: A DOI (title checked against Crossref) or a US label on DailyMed (setid checked to resolve), each cited with what it says. ChEMBL and GtoPdb, the score's inputs, and DrugBank and Wikipedia were not allowed. Labels and reviews restate mechanism knowledge ChEMBL's curators also read, so this key is not independent of the score as the label key is: what it adds is negatives, opposites and pre-registration.
provenance.seen: true where the probe set (analysis/probe/probes.mjs) already put the same relationship to the ranking, so its answer was known before this key existed.
provenance.doubt: Set where a drafter or the reviewer judged the sourcing or the claim weaker than the rest: a class-level source, a mechanism a label calls unknown, an indication that overlaps rather than matches. Doubted pairs stay in and are graded both ways.
